title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of political impersonation carried out with a generative video tool. The videos placed fabricated speech into the mouth of a candidate who never said those words, and they were published to a public social media account as campaign content. The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation: the tool produced the clips, and a person or campaign chose to post them.

The label identifying the videos as AI-generated was applied automatically by the generator, which means the disclosure came from the tooling rather than from the person distributing the material. Catching this before publication would have required the poster to treat a synthetic clip of a real person saying something they never said as something not to publish, or the platform to treat it as such. No automated check appears in the reporting to have done either.

What is established is that a cease-and-desist letter was sent, that it asserts the videos are fiction and could violate state defamation law, and that the campaign rejected the demand. Whether the videos are defamatory, whether any law was broken, and whether the poster intended to deceive are not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared Aug. 4. The videos carry an automatic label noting they were made with an AI generator called Grok Imagine.

Cooke's attorney, Ben Stafford, wrote on Sept. 30 that the videos are fiction and could violate state defamation law. The letter says Cooke's attorneys are monitoring Van Orden's accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden's campaign called Cooke's action a tantrum, and he responded with another AI video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!" Cooke lost to Van Orden by about 3 points in 2024.
